observation_summary: The GJChronology class fails to handle the transition across the 1 BC / 1 AD boundary because it does not account for the non-existence of year 0. When performing arithmetic that crosses this boundary, the code produces an invalid year 0, triggering an IllegalFieldValueException.
hypothesis: The GJChronology implementation fails to account for the non-existence of year 0 in the Julian/Gregorian calendar transition when performing date arithmetic (like plusYears or plusWeekyears) that crosses the 1 BC / 1 AD boundary. The logic in ImpreciseCutoverField.add does not check if the resulting year is 0 and adjust it accordingly, leading to an IllegalFieldValueException when the underlying chronology attempts to process the invalid year 0.
prediction: The code in ImpreciseCutoverField.add (lines 973-991) performs arithmetic across the cutover point without checking if the resulting year is 0. I expect that adding a check to adjust the year by -1 if it results in 0 will resolve the IllegalFieldValueException.

The snippet of ImpreciseCutoverField.add confirms that it performs arithmetic and then calls gregorianToJulian, which eventually triggers the conversion logic that fails on year 0. The fix requires adding a guard condition to detect and skip year 0.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a missing validation/adjustment for the year 0 boundary in the GJChronology arithmetic logic. The code performs arithmetic and then converts between chronologies without checking if the resulting year is valid (i.e., not 0). This is a classic 'Checking' defect where the logic fails to validate the boundary condition of the calendar system.
